Clubs & Activities

Beyond the classroom

Student clubs that put values into practice.

Ebenezer's student clubs give learners a hands-on way to act on what they study — from community outreach to caring for the campus grounds.

Peace and Humanity Club

March with Madan

Members took part in a community outreach event, marching together for peace and humanitarian awareness.

Environmental Health Protection Club

Keeping the campus clean

Members sweep, clear, and tidy the school grounds and corridors as a regular part of the club's work.

Agriculture Club

Planting on campus

The Agriculture Club plants and tends flower beds around the school buildings.

Interact Club

Ebenezer's chapter of a worldwide service network

Interact is Rotary International's service club for young people ages 12–18, sponsored and mentored by a local Rotary club. Chapters run at least two projects a year — one for their own school or community, one with an international focus — while members build leadership and public-speaking skills along the way. The Ebenezer chapter kicked off its year with a "Welcome Back to School" recruitment drive, inviting students to a general meeting in the school hall.

Anti-Corruption Club

Small choice, big impact

Students in the Anti-Corruption Club use awareness events to talk through honesty and accountability — both in school life and beyond it.

Science Club

Teaching computer science, CS50-style

Inspired by Harvard's CS50 introduction to computer science, Science Club members put together their own beginner sessions for junior students, walking them through the basics on the school's computers and presenting what they'd learned to the group.

Red Cross Club

A blood donation program on campus

Working with the Red Cross, the club organised a blood donation drive at school, with staff and volunteer donors from the student body taking part.

More club photos are on their way — this page will grow as new activities are added.
